steps.text: Cook the rice in 150 ml water, covered, then keep it warm in a tiffin.
Whisk the besan with 250 ml water, turmeric and salt into a smooth thin batter.
Heat oil, pop the mustard and cumin seeds, then add garlic, chilli and onion.
When the onion softens, pour in the besan batter while stirring.
Keep stirring on medium-low until thick and glossy and the raw besan taste is gone.
Top with coriander and eat with rice.

tip.text: Raw besan tastes bitter and powdery. Cook until the pitla stops sticking to the spoon.

steps.text: Dry-roast the besan in the pan on low, stirring, until it turns a shade darker and smells nutty. Tip it out.
Heat oil, add cumin and the capsicum strips.
Stir-fry until the capsicum softens but keeps some crunch.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt.
Sprinkle the roasted besan over and toss until it coats the capsicum like a dry crumble.
Warm the wraps for 20 seconds a side and eat the sabzi rolled inside.

tip.text: Roasting the besan first is the whole trick. Raw besan here sticks and tastes raw.

steps.text: Chop the tomatoes into small pieces.
Heat oil, pop mustard and cumin, then add hing.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder and salt.
Cook until the tomatoes turn soft and saucy.
Stir in the jaggery and 50 ml water and simmer 2 minutes.
Switch off and top with a handful of sev and coriander right before eating.

tip.text: The sev goes in at the table. Add it in the pan and it turns into soft mush.

steps.text: Cook the rice with 300 ml water and keep it covered.
Put the dal, chopped tomatoes, green chilli, turmeric and 450 ml water in the pan and simmer until mushy.
Mash it well with the spoon and season with salt and chilli powder.
Heat oil in a ladle over the plate, add mustard, cumin, crushed garlic and curry leaves until the garlic browns.
Pour the tempering into the dal.
Mix a spoon of ghee or oil into hot rice and eat it with the pappu.

tip.text: Let the garlic go properly brown in the tempering. That nutty garlic is the Andhra flavour.

steps.text: Dry-roast the desiccated coconut on low until deep brown, stirring all the time. Tip it out.
Crush the roasted coconut with the coriander and chilli powder in a folded paper.
Heat oil, pop mustard seeds, add curry leaves, onion, ginger and garlic and cook until soft.
Add the tomato and the coconut-spice mix and fry 2 minutes.
Add the rinsed chickpeas and 250 ml water and simmer until the gravy turns dark and thick.
Finish with garam masala and eat with pav or rice.

tip.text: Roasted coconut goes from brown to burnt in seconds. Stay at the pan and keep stirring.

steps.text: Quarter the mushrooms and sear them in half the oil on high until browned. Take them out.
Heat the remaining oil, add cumin and cook the onion until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, tomato and spice powders and cook down into a thick masala.
Return the mushrooms with any juice and add 80 ml water.
Simmer so the mushrooms absorb the masala.
Stir in the cream and garam masala.

tip.text: Searing first keeps mushrooms meaty. Simmered raw, they turn into slippery slices.

steps.text: Wipe the mushrooms clean and slice them about 5 mm thick.
Heat oil, add cumin and cook the onion until golden.
Add tomato, turmeric and chilli powder and cook until mushy.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the whisked curd, then put it back on.
Add the peas, mushrooms and 100 ml water and simmer until the peas are tender.
Finish with garam masala and crushed kasuri methi.

tip.text: Curd added to a sizzling pan curdles. Take the pan off the heat for 30 seconds first.

steps.text: Rinse the chickpeas and chop the spinach finely.
Heat oil, add cumin and the onion and garlic, and cook until golden.
Add tomato and spice powders and cook until thick.
Add the chickpeas and 150 ml water and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook until it collapses into the gravy.
Finish with garam masala and lemon.

tip.text: Spinach goes in last. Cook it too long and it turns dark olive and loses its iron-y freshness.

steps.text: Simmer the rinsed moong dal with 500 ml water and turmeric until soft.
Add the chopped spinach and salt and cook 3 more minutes.
Whisk the dal so the spinach breaks up through it. Pour it into a bowl.
Heat ghee in the pan, add cumin and lots of sliced garlic and fry until golden.
Add the onion and chilli powder and fry 1 minute.
Pour the dal back over the tempering, stir and simmer 2 minutes.

tip.text: Golden garlic in ghee is the flavour here. Pull it off the moment it turns golden, it goes bitter fast.

steps.text: Cut the potato and carrot into small cubes and the beans into short pieces.
Heat oil, add curry leaves, slit chilli, ginger and sliced onion and cook until soft but not brown.
Add the vegetables, salt and 200 ml water.
Cover and simmer until the potato is tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and pepper and warm it through gently.
Ladle the stew into a bowl and dunk pav into it, or pour it over rice.

tip.text: Boiling coconut milk makes it split and grainy. Warm it just until steaming.

steps.text: Cook the rice with 150 ml water and keep it covered.
Cut the thawed basa into large chunks and rub with salt and turmeric.
Heat oil and cook curry leaves, onion, ginger and garlic until soft.
Add the chilli and coriander powders, then the tomato, and cook until soft.
Add 100 ml water and bring to a simmer, then slide the fish in.
Cook gently without stirring until the fish turns opaque.
Pour in the coconut milk, warm through, add lemon and spoon over rice.

tip.text: Stirring breaks the soft basa into flakes. Shake the pan instead.

steps.text: Thaw the basa fully and pat it very dry with a cloth.
Mix chilli powder, turmeric, grated garlic and ginger, lemon juice and salt into a paste.
Rub the paste over the fish and leave it.
Press both sides of the fillet into the rava.
Shallow-fry in hot oil until crisp, then flip carefully once.
Eat with onion rings and a squeeze of lemon.

tip.text: Frozen basa holds a lot of water. If you don't dry it, the rava coating peels off in the pan.

steps.text: Wash the rice and soak it. Meanwhile marinate the chicken in curd, chilli powder, half the garam masala, ginger, garlic, turmeric and salt.
Slice the onions thin and fry them in ghee and oil until dark golden. Lift out half for topping.
Add the tomato, green chilli and chicken with its marinade and cook on high until the chicken turns white.
Spread the drained rice over the chicken in an even layer without stirring.
Pour 330 ml hot water gently over the rice, add salt, mint, lemon juice and the remaining garam masala.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat.
Switch off and let it rest with the lid closed, then fold gently from the bottom and top with the fried onions.

tip.text: Never stir the layers. Stirring makes it pulao, and the bottom chicken burns while the rice above is raw.

steps.text: Cut the chicken into thin strips and coat with curd, chilli powder, garam masala and salt.
Stir-fry the chicken in hot oil until browned and cooked through. Take it out.
Beat the egg with a pinch of salt. Pour half into the pan and press a wrap on top.
When the egg sets, flip to warm the wrap. Repeat with the second wrap.
Slice the onion thin and mix with lemon and chopped chilli.
Fill each egg-wrap with chicken, onion and ketchup and roll it in paper.

tip.text: Thin strips cook in 6 minutes and stay juicy. Big pieces dry out on the outside before the centre is done.

steps.text: Cut the paneer into fingers and coat them in curd, chilli powder and salt.
Fry them in the hot pan until charred in spots on two sides.
Add capsicum strips for the last minute so they soften slightly.
Warm each wrap in the dry pan for 20 seconds per side.
Toss sliced onion with lemon and chaat masala.
Fill the wraps with paneer, capsicum, onion and ketchup and roll tight.

tip.text: Leave the paneer alone to char. Moving it every few seconds means no colour.

steps.text: Boil the potato cubes in the pan until very soft, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Drain and mash with chilli, grated ginger, chaat masala and salt.
Shape into 2 thick patties the width of your pav and coat them in rava.
Shallow-fry in hot oil until golden and crisp, then flip.
Slit and toast the pav in the same pan.
Sandwich each tikki in a pav with ketchup and raw onion.

tip.text: If the mash is too wet the tikki falls apart. Let the potato steam dry before mashing.

steps.text: Boil the potato cubes until soft.
Drain and mash the potato with pav bhaji masala, grated jaggery, lemon and salt.
Heat oil and fry the mash for 3 minutes so the masala cooks in, then spread it flat in the pan.
Top the potato with peanuts and pomegranate while it's still in the pan, then scoop out.
Slit the pav, fill with the potato, then onion and a lot of sev, pressing the sides in.
Toast the stuffed pav in butter on both sides.

tip.text: Press sev onto the open sides of the filled pav. That crunchy edge is what makes it dabeli.

steps.text: Melt the butter in the pan and add the finely chopped onion and capsicum.
Add the tomato, pav bhaji masala, chilli powder and salt and cook until mushy.
Squeeze lemon into the masala and add coriander.
Slit the pav horizontally and open it like a book.
Press both cut sides into the masala in the pan so they soak it up.
Toast until the pav is crisp at the edges and coated red.

tip.text: Press the pav into the masala in the pan, don't spoon it in. That's how it soaks up the butter.

steps.text: Cook the washed rice with 180 ml water and cool it on a plate.
Heat oil and fry the cashews until golden.
Add mustard seeds, hing, curry leaves and slit chilli.
Add the desiccated coconut and stir on low until it just turns light golden.
Tip in the rice and salt and fold until every grain is coated.

tip.text: Coconut catches very fast. Stay on low and stir the whole time.

steps.text: Boil 1 litre of water with a teaspoon of salt and cook the penne, stirring once or twice, until it has a slight bite.
Keep a cup of the pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Heat oil in the same pan and cook the onion, capsicum and corn for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato, chilli powder and garam masala and cook until saucy.
Stir in the ketchup, oregano and a splash of pasta water.
Toss the pasta through the masala and tear the cheese slice over the top to melt.

tip.text: Pasta water should taste salty like the sea. It's the only chance the pasta gets to be seasoned inside.

steps.text: Cook the penne in plenty of salted boiling water until al dente.
Scoop out half a cup of the starchy pasta water before you drain.
Warm the olive oil and fry the sliced garlic until just golden at the edges.
Add the pasta sauce and oregano and simmer 2 minutes.
Add the pasta and a splash of pasta water and toss until the sauce clings to every piece.
Top with grated mozzarella and cover for a minute to melt.

tip.text: That splash of starchy water turns a watery jar sauce into a glossy one that sticks. Don't skip it.

steps.text: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water, drain and set it aside in a tiffin.
Melt the butter on low heat and fry the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the atta and stir for a minute until it smells biscuity.
Pour in the milk a little at a time, whisking after each pour so no lumps form.
Add corn, capsicum, salt and pepper and simmer until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Stir in the cheese slice and oregano, then fold in the pasta.

tip.text: All the milk at once makes lumpy sauce. Pour in four rounds and whisk every time.

steps.text: Cook the pasta in well-salted water until just al dente.
Save a cup of the pasta water and drain.
Heat the olive oil gently and add the thinly sliced garlic and chilli flakes.
Stir until the garlic is pale gold, then pour in 4 tablespoons of pasta water so it sizzles and stops cooking.
Add the pasta and toss hard until the oil and water turn into a light sauce.
Finish with chopped coriander standing in for parsley and a squeeze of lemon.

tip.text: Brown garlic is bitter garlic. Pull it at pale gold and the pasta water stops it in its tracks.

steps.text: Beat the eggs in a bowl with the torn cheese slices and lots of black pepper.
Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente and keep half a cup of the water.
Slice the sausage into coins and fry in butter until browned.
Switch off the induction plate completely and wait 30 seconds.
Add the drained pasta to the sausage, then pour in the egg mix with 3 tablespoons of pasta water.
Toss quickly for a minute until the sauce turns creamy from the leftover heat.

tip.text: Pour the eggs in on a live plate and you get scrambled egg pasta. The heat must be off.

steps.text: Cook the penne in salted water and drain, keeping a little of the water.
Warm the olive oil and cook the chopped onion and garlic until soft.
Add the chopped tomato and oregano and cook into a chunky sauce.
Flake in the drained tuna and stir gently to warm it.
Toss in the pasta with a splash of pasta water.
Squeeze a little lemon over the top.

tip.text: Canned tuna is already cooked. Long simmering only dries it out and makes it fishy.

steps.text: Put the pasta in the pan with 300 ml water, 150 ml milk and a pinch of salt.
Simmer, stirring often, until the pasta is soft and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Turn the heat to low and add the butter.
Tear in the cheese slices one at a time, stirring until each melts.
Season with pepper and oregano and eat it while it's gooey.

tip.text: Milk catches on the base. Stir every minute and keep the heat at medium.

steps.text: Cook the pasta in salted water and drain.
Cut the chicken into small pieces and season with salt and half the chilli flakes.
Sear the chicken in olive oil on high until browned and cooked through.
Add the garlic and the rest of the chilli and fry 30 seconds.
Pour in the pasta sauce and simmer 2 minutes.
Toss in the pasta and top with mozzarella.

tip.text: Pat the chicken dry before searing. Wet chicken boils grey instead of browning.

steps.text: Cook the pasta in well-salted water until al dente.
Grate the zucchini on the large holes of a grater.
Heat the olive oil and cook the garlic and chilli for 30 seconds.
Add the zucchini and cook on high until most of its water steams away.
Add the pasta, lemon zest and juice, and a little pasta water and toss.
Finish with mozzarella and black pepper.

tip.text: Zucchini is mostly water. High heat drives it off. On low you get a puddle.

steps.text: Cook the pasta in salted water and drain.
Slice the sausages into coins and fry until browned on both sides.
Add the onion and pepper strips and cook until soft and slightly charred.
Pour in the pasta sauce and oregano and bubble for 2 minutes.
Fold the drained pasta through the sausage and pepper sauce.

tip.text: Sausages already have fat. Use only a little oil or the pan turns greasy.

steps.text: Boil the noodles in salted water, stirring to separate, until just tender.
Drain, rinse under cold water and toss with a few drops of oil.
Shred the cabbage and cut the carrot and capsicum into thin strips.
Heat oil on maximum, add garlic, then all the vegetables and toss for 90 seconds.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, salt, sugar and pepper and toss with two spoons for a minute.
Add spring onion and switch off.

tip.text: Skipping the cold rinse means the noodles keep cooking and clump into a solid brick.

steps.text: Boil the noodles until tender, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Scramble the beaten eggs in hot oil until set, break them up and push them to one side.
Add the sliced onion, capsicum, carrot and green chilli and stir-fry on high for a minute.
Add the noodles, soy sauce and salt and toss together with the egg.
Squirt in ketchup and toss again. Kolkata chowmein is always a little sweet-sour.

tip.text: Ketchup goes in last and briefly. It caramelises and sticks if it cooks too long.

steps.text: Cook the noodles until just tender, then drain and rinse in cold water.
Heat oil on high, add garlic and the sliced vegetables and stir-fry for a minute.
Add the schezwan chutney and fry 20 seconds until the oil turns red.
Add the noodles and soy sauce and toss until coated evenly.
Finish with spring onion and eat hot.

tip.text: Frying the schezwan chutney briefly in oil releases the chilli flavour into the noodles.

steps.text: Cook the Maggi in 250 ml water in the pan with half the tastemaker until almost dry.
Let the noodles cool for 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the rest of the tastemaker, onion and chilli, then mix in the noodles.
Heat oil in the pan and pour in the mixture, pressing it flat.
Cook on medium-low until the base is golden.
Flip it using a plate, lay the cheese on top and cover for a minute to melt.

tip.text: Slide it onto a plate, cover with the pan and flip together. A spatula flip will tear it.

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, add chilli and the onion and fry until soft.
Add tomato, capsicum, peas and chilli powder and cook 2 minutes.
Pour in 300 ml water with the tastemaker and bring to a boil.
Add the noodle cake and cook, loosening the strands with a fork.
Cook until the water mostly disappears and the noodles look glossy.

tip.text: Some like it soupy, some dry. Take it off a minute early for soupy.

steps.text: Bring 400 ml water to a boil with the grated garlic, chilli powder, soy sauce and sugar.
Add the noodle cake without the tastemaker and cook until the strands loosen.
Crack the egg into the broth and don't stir.
Cover so the egg poaches on top of the noodles.
Slide into a bowl, lay the cheese slice on top to melt and finish with spring onion and sesame.

tip.text: Cheese in ramen sounds wrong but is very Korean. It mellows the chilli heat.

steps.text: Soak or boil the noodles until just soft, then drain and rinse cold.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, grated jaggery, lemon juice and 3 tablespoons of hot water into a sauce.
Heat oil and fry the garlic, then scramble the egg in the same pan.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss on high until the sauce is absorbed.
Throw in the sprouts and spring onion and toss for 30 seconds.
Top with crushed peanuts, chilli flakes and a wedge of lemon.

tip.text: Taste the sauce before it goes in: it should be sweet, salty and sour all at once. Adjust with lemon or jaggery.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 170 ml water, covered on low, then transfer to a bowl.
Mix soy sauce, honey, grated garlic, ginger and 2 tablespoons of water.
Cut the chicken into thin strips and sear in hot oil until browned.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble until thick and sticky, turning the chicken.
Spoon the chicken and glaze over the rice.
Add cucumber slices, sesame and spring onion.

tip.text: Honey burns quickly. Lower the heat once the sauce goes in and keep the chicken moving.

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it in a covered bowl.
Simmer 100 ml water with soy sauce and sugar in the pan.
Add the thinly sliced onion and cook until soft.
Add the chicken in small pieces and simmer until cooked through.
Pour the lightly beaten eggs over in a circle, cover and cook just until barely set.
Slide everything over the rice and scatter spring onion.

tip.text: Barely beat the eggs. You want streaks of white and yolk, not a uniform omelette.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and leave it to drain.
Heat oil and fry the dry rice until some grains turn chalky white and toasty.
Add onion, garlic, cumin and chilli powder and stir 1 minute.
Add the finely chopped tomato, corn, capsicum, salt and 160 ml water.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat.
Fluff and finish with lemon and coriander.

tip.text: Toasting the rice in oil first is what makes Mexican rice fluffy and separate.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 150 ml water and stir in half the lemon juice. Tip it into a bowl.
Heat oil and fry the cumin, chilli powder and half the onion for a minute.
Add the rinsed rajma, corn, salt and a splash of water and cook until thick.
Mix the rest of the onion with the chopped tomato and lemon for a salsa.
Shred the lettuce into thin ribbons for crunch.
Build the bowl: rice, beans, salsa, lettuce and a spoon of curd.

tip.text: Mash a few beans as they cook. It makes them cling together like refried beans.

steps.text: Melt half the butter and fry the sliced mushrooms until golden. Take them out.
Add the rest of the butter, the chopped onion and garlic and cook until soft.
Add the unwashed rice and stir for a minute so it turns glossy.
Add 150 ml hot water and stir often until absorbed, then another 150 ml, and keep going.
When the rice is creamy but still has a little bite, stir in the milk and the cheese slice.
Fold in the mushrooms and season with salt and plenty of pepper.

tip.text: Don't wash the rice for this one. The surface starch is what makes it creamy.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 160 ml water and spread it on a plate to cool.
Cut the chicken small and stir-fry on high with garlic until cooked through.
Push the chicken aside and scramble the egg in the gap.
Add the diced carrot and toss for a minute.
Add the rice, soy sauce, salt and pepper and toss on high.
Fold in the spring onion and switch off while it is still bright green.

tip.text: Keep the chicken pieces small, the size of a fingernail, so they cook as fast as everything else.

steps.text: Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve, rubbing it, until the water stops foaming.
Heat ghee, add cumin and onion and cook until golden.
Add the vegetables and garam masala and stir 2 minutes.
Add the quinoa and 160 ml water with salt.
Cover and simmer on low until the water is absorbed and each grain shows a little white tail.
Rest 5 minutes covered, then fluff with lemon juice and serve with curd.

tip.text: Unrinsed quinoa tastes soapy and bitter. Rinse until the foam is gone.

steps.text: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it with 140 ml water, covered, until absorbed. Tip it into a bowl.
Rub the chicken with garlic, oregano, salt, pepper and half the lemon juice.
Sear the chicken in half the olive oil until golden and cooked through, turning once.
Let it rest 3 minutes, then slice it.
Toss the quinoa with chopped cucumber, tomato, mint, the rest of the lemon and oil.
Lay the chicken slices on top.

tip.text: Slicing chicken straight off the pan lets the juice run out. Three minutes of rest keeps it moist.

steps.text: Rinse the rajma and mash it with chilli powder, crushed cumin and salt.
Spread the mash over half of each wrap.
Scatter onion, capsicum and grated cheese over the beans, then fold the wraps in half.
Brush the pan with oil and lay the quesadillas in.
Press with a spatula and toast until golden and the cheese starts to ooze.
Flip, toast the other side, cut into wedges and dip into curd.

tip.text: Medium heat, not high. The outside burns before the cheese melts if you rush it.

steps.text: Cut the chicken, pepper and onion into thin strips.
Toss the chicken with chilli powder, crushed cumin, salt and lemon juice.
Stir-fry the chicken on high until cooked, then add the vegetables for 2 minutes.
Tip the filling out and wipe the pan.
Fill half of each wrap with chicken and cheese and fold.
Toast both sides until crisp and melted.

tip.text: Wipe the pan before toasting. Leftover juices make the wraps soggy instead of crisp.

steps.text: Warm the baked beans in the pan with chilli powder, then tip them into a bowl.
Heat oil, add the onion, then the beaten eggs with salt.
Scramble gently until soft curds form.
Warm the wrap in the dry pan for 20 seconds a side so it bends without cracking.
Lay the cheese slice on the wrap, then the eggs and beans.
Fold the sides in, roll it up and toast the seam side down for 30 seconds to seal.

tip.text: Toasting the seam first glues the burrito shut so it doesn't unroll.

steps.text: Heat oil and cook the onion and garlic until soft.
Add the cumin, chilli powder and oregano and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato and cook down until thick.
Add the rajma, corn, salt and 150 ml water and simmer until thick and rich.
Mash a quarter of the beans into the sauce.
Eat in a bowl topped with curd, with tortilla chips for scooping.

tip.text: Real chili is thick enough to stand a spoon in. If it's soupy, simmer it longer with the lid off.

steps.text: Toss the paneer cubes in besan, salt and a teaspoon of water so they're lightly coated.
Shallow-fry them in hot oil until golden on two sides. Take them out.
In the same oil, stir-fry garlic and slit chilli, then the onion and capsicum squares on high for a minute.
Add soy sauce, ketchup, sugar and 3 tablespoons of water.
Return the paneer and toss until glossy.
Finish with spring onion greens.

tip.text: Onion and capsicum should stay crunchy. One minute on high heat, no more.

steps.text: Cut the potatoes into thin fingers and soak them in water for 10 minutes to remove starch.
Drain, pat completely dry and toss with besan and salt, then shallow-fry in batches until crisp.
Pour out most of the oil, leaving a spoonful, and fry garlic and chilli flakes.
Add soy sauce and honey and let it bubble for 20 seconds.
Toss the potatoes in the glaze.
Sprinkle sesame and spring onion.

tip.text: Dry potatoes go crisp. Wet ones splatter and stay limp.

steps.text: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and coat with egg, besan, half the soy sauce, salt and pepper.
Shallow-fry in hot oil until crisp and cooked through, turning once.
Lift out the chicken and pour off all but a spoon of oil.
Stir-fry the garlic and chilli, then the onion and capsicum squares on high for a minute.
Add the rest of the soy sauce, ketchup and 2 tablespoons of water.
Toss the chicken through and finish with spring onion.

tip.text: Fry in two batches if the pan is crowded, or the coating turns soggy.

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs in the pan, cool them in water and peel.
Cut each egg into quarters and dust lightly with besan.
Fry the egg pieces gently in hot oil until the outside is golden. Take them out.
Stir-fry the garlic, chilli, onion and capsicum on high.
Add soy sauce, schezwan and ketchup with a splash of water.
Fold the eggs in carefully so the yolks stay attached.

tip.text: Fold, don't stir. Rough stirring pops the yolks out.

steps.text: Crush half the corn kernels with the back of a spoon to release their milky juice.
Simmer all the corn in 350 ml water with salt and sugar.
Mix the besan with 3 tablespoons of cold water until smooth and stir it into the soup to thicken it.
Beat the egg and pour it into the simmering soup in a thin stream while stirring slowly.
Add soy sauce and pepper and switch off.
Ladle into a bowl and top with sliced spring onion.

tip.text: Pour slowly and stir in one direction for silky ribbons. Dump it in and you get scrambled egg lumps.

steps.text: Slice the chicken very thin and crush the garlic and ginger.
Simmer the garlic and ginger in 500 ml water for a quick broth.
Add the chicken and simmer until white and cooked through.
Add the thinly sliced carrot and cabbage and cook until just tender.
Season with salt, pepper and soy sauce.
Squeeze in a little lemon and top with spring onion.

tip.text: Keep it at a gentle simmer. A rolling boil makes the broth cloudy and the chicken tough.

steps.text: Press the tofu in a cloth, cut it into cubes and toss in besan.
Fry the tofu in hot oil until golden on most sides. Take it out.
Add the broccoli florets and capsicum with 2 tablespoons of water and cover for 2 minutes.
Uncover, add lots of sliced garlic and fry until fragrant.
Add soy sauce and honey, return the tofu and toss.
Sprinkle sesame seeds over the tofu and eat it hot.

tip.text: The splash of water and lid steam the broccoli. Without it, the outside burns while the stalks stay raw.

steps.text: Shred the cabbage as thin as you can with a sharp knife.
Scramble the eggs in half the oil until just set, then take them out.
Heat the rest of the oil on high and fry the garlic for 10 seconds.
Add the cabbage and toss constantly until it wilts but stays crunchy.
Add soy sauce and pepper, then return the egg.
Toss once more with spring onion.

tip.text: High heat and constant tossing. On low the cabbage stews and turns watery.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 150 ml water and keep it covered in a tiffin.
Slice the chicken thin and toss with besan and a little soy sauce.
Sear the chicken on high until browned and cooked. Take it out.
Add the broccoli and 3 tablespoons of water, cover and steam.
Add garlic and ginger, then the chicken, the rest of the soy sauce and honey.
Toss until glossy, sprinkle sesame and spoon over rice.

tip.text: The besan coating gives the sauce something to cling to.

steps.text: Butterfly the chicken breast so it's even in thickness, then season with salt, pepper and oregano.
Sear in half the butter on medium-high until golden on one side, then flip.
Cover and cook the second side until there's no pink inside. Rest it on a plate.
Add the rest of the butter and the sliced mushrooms and brown them.
Add the garlic and spinach, then the cream, and simmer 1 minute.
Slice the chicken and pour the sauce over.

tip.text: Uneven chicken breast cooks dry at the thin end and raw at the thick end. Butterfly or pound it flat.

steps.text: Boil the potato in chunks until soft, mash with half the butter and salt, and keep it covered.
Pound the chicken flat between two sheets of plastic with the bottom of a glass.
Season with salt and half the pepper.
Sear in oil and butter until golden and cooked through, turning once.
Lower the heat, add garlic, the rest of the coarse pepper and the cream, and simmer 1 minute.
Plate the mash, lay the steak on it and pour the pepper sauce over.

tip.text: Crush peppercorns coarse for steak sauce. Fine pepper powder makes it gritty and harsh.

steps.text: Cut the paneer into two thick slabs and season with salt, pepper and oregano.
Sear in butter on medium-high until golden-brown, then flip.
Take the paneer out and add the chopped vegetables and garlic to the pan.
Toss on high until the vegetables are crisp-tender.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon.
Put the vegetables on a plate and top with the paneer slabs.

tip.text: Don't move the paneer while it sears. It sticks at first and releases once it's browned.

steps.text: Boil the potato chunks until soft, then mash with milk, half the butter and salt. Keep it covered.
Pat the basa completely dry and season with salt and pepper.
Fry it in the rest of the butter until golden underneath, then flip carefully.
Add garlic and the juice of the lemon to the butter and spoon it over the fish.
Lift the fish out and wilt the spinach in the leftover butter for a minute.
Plate the mash, spinach and fish and pour the pan butter over.

tip.text: Use a wide spatula and turn the fish only once. Basa flakes apart easily.

steps.text: Butter the bread and toast it in the pan until crisp on both sides. Put it on a plate.
Tip the baked beans into the pan and warm them until bubbling gently.
Stir a small knob of butter into the beans for gloss.
Pour the beans over the toast.
Tear the cheese slice over the hot beans and grind black pepper on top.

tip.text: Beans catch and burn at the edges. Stir them every 30 seconds.

steps.text: Spread pasta sauce over each slice of bread.
Top with capsicum, onion and corn, then a generous layer of mozzarella.
Sprinkle oregano and chilli flakes.
Rub butter on the pan and set the slices in on low heat.
Cover with a lid and cook until the cheese melts and the base is crisp.

tip.text: Low heat and a lid is your oven. High heat burns the base before the cheese melts.

steps.text: Mash the butter with finely grated garlic and oregano.
Spread the garlic butter over one side of each slice.
Pile the mozzarella on the buttered side.
Place the slices in a cold pan, cheese side up, and put it on medium-low heat.
Cover and cook until the cheese has melted and the base is crisp.

tip.text: Starting in a cold pan gives the cheese time to melt before the base burns.

steps.text: Butter one side of each slice of bread right to the edges.
Place one slice butter side down in the pan and layer the cheese slices, tomato and mozzarella on it.
Close with the second slice, butter side up.
Cook on medium-low, pressing gently, until deep golden underneath.
Flip and cook the other side until the cheese oozes.

tip.text: Low and slow. Medium-low heat lets the cheese melt fully before the bread burns.

steps.text: Boil the potato in slices in the pan until soft, then drain.
Chop the mint, coriander, green chilli and salt very fine together for a quick green chutney.
Butter all three slices of bread and spread chutney on two.
Layer potato, tomato, cucumber and onion on one chutney slice with chaat masala, then the plain slice, then cheese and the last chutney slice.
Toast the stack in butter in the pan, pressing with a spatula, until crisp on both sides.
Cut into four and dust with more chaat masala.

tip.text: Press the sandwich down with a steel plate or a pan of water. It holds the layers together.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in salted simmering water until cooked through.
Let the chicken cool, then shred it with two forks.
Mix the shredded chicken with mayo, finely chopped onion, salt and pepper.
Toast the bread in butter in the pan.
Fill with lettuce and the chicken mayo and cut in half.

tip.text: Gentle simmering keeps the chicken soft. Boiling hard makes it stringy and dry.

steps.text: Wilt the chopped spinach with garlic in half the butter for a minute.
Add the corn, salt and pepper and cook until any water dries up.
Mix the spinach and corn with the mozzarella in a bowl.
Spread the filling between the bread slices.
Toast in the remaining butter, pressing down, until golden and melted.

tip.text: Cook off the spinach water completely or the sandwich turns soggy inside.

steps.text: Drain the tuna and mix it with mayo, chopped onion and pepper.
Butter the outside of both slices of bread.
Lay one slice butter side down in the pan, add a cheese slice, the tuna, then the second cheese slice.
Close with the second piece of bread, butter side up.
Toast on medium-low until golden, then flip and toast until the cheese melts.

tip.text: Cheese on both sides of the tuna acts like glue and stops the filling sliding out.

steps.text: Rinse the chickpeas and pat them very dry.
Fry them in oil with crushed cumin, chilli powder, turmeric and salt until they crackle and crisp.
Stir half the grated garlic and a squeeze of lemon into the curd for a garlic sauce.
Warm the wrap in the pan until soft and slightly blistered.
Spread the garlic sauce, add lettuce, tomato, onion and the hot chickpeas.
Roll it tight in a piece of foil or paper.

tip.text: Chickpeas pop in hot oil. Keep a lid nearby and cover partly while they crisp.

steps.text: Simmer the crushed garlic and ginger in 600 ml water.
Add the thinly sliced chicken and carrot and simmer until cooked.
Drop in the noodles and cook until soft.
Season with soy sauce, salt and pepper.
Pour into a big bowl and top with spring onion and a squeeze of lemon.

tip.text: Noodles soak up broth as they sit. Add an extra 100 ml water if you're eating slowly.

steps.text: Simmer 400 ml water with sliced ginger, crushed garlic and slit chillies.
Add the sliced mushrooms and tomato wedges.
Simmer until the mushrooms are soft.
Season with soy sauce and sugar.
Switch off and squeeze in the whole lemon.
Top with coriander and spring onion.

tip.text: Lemon juice boiled hard turns bitter. Add it after switching off for that bright sour hit.

steps.text: Chop all the vegetables very fine.
Fry the garlic and ginger in oil for 30 seconds, then add the vegetables for a minute.
Add 400 ml water, soy sauce and salt and simmer.
Stir in the besan mixed with 3 tablespoons of cold water and simmer until slightly thick.
Add plenty of black pepper and the lemon juice.
Pour into a bowl and finish with chopped spring onion.

tip.text: Pepper is the hot, lemon is the sour. Taste and push both until it's punchy.

steps.text: Cut the baby corn into halves lengthways and blanch in boiling water for 2 minutes.
Drain, pat dry and toss with besan, salt and a few drops of water.
Shallow-fry until crisp on the cut sides.
Push aside and stir-fry garlic, onion and capsicum on high for a minute.
Add soy sauce and lots of pepper and toss everything together.
Scatter spring onion greens over the corn before serving.

tip.text: Blanching first means the corn is tender inside by the time the outside is crisp.

steps.text: Melt the butter and cook the chopped onion and garlic until soft.
Add the chopped tomatoes, salt and sugar and cook until they collapse completely.
Add 200 ml water and simmer 5 minutes.
Mash hard with a steel glass, then pour through a sieve into a bowl, pressing the pulp through.
Return to the pan, warm it, and stir in pepper and cream.
Cut the bread into cubes and toast in the dry pan as croutons.

tip.text: No blender? A sieve and a spoon give you smooth soup. It takes 2 minutes of pressing.

steps.text: Chop the mushrooms very fine on a board.
Melt butter and cook the onion, garlic and mushrooms until the mushroom water evaporates.
Sprinkle the atta over and stir 1 minute.
Add 150 ml water, then the milk, a little at a time, stirring.
Simmer gently until thick and creamy.
Season with salt, pepper and oregano.

tip.text: Wait for the mushrooms to stop releasing water and start to brown. That's where the deep flavour comes from.

steps.text: Melt the butter and fry half the garlic sliced thin until golden. Lift it out for topping.
Add the rest of the garlic, chopped, with the onion and cumin and cook until soft.
Add the spinach and 200 ml water and simmer until very soft.
Mash thoroughly with a masher or steel glass until the spinach is broken down.
Stir in the milk, warm through, and season with salt, pepper and lemon.
Top with the crisp garlic slices.

tip.text: Don't boil after adding milk and lemon together. Warm it through, then add the lemon in the bowl.

steps.text: Cut the sausages diagonally into thick slices.
Fry them in oil until well browned.
Add the sliced onion and pepper and cook until soft with charred edges.
Add garlic, oregano and ketchup and toss.
Pile onto toasted bread or eat as is.

tip.text: Diagonal slices give more surface to brown, and more flavour.

steps.text: Cut the broccoli into small florets and the paneer into cubes.
Sear the paneer in half the oil until golden. Take it out.
Add the broccoli with 3 tablespoons of water, cover and steam.
Uncover, add the rest of the oil and lots of sliced garlic and fry until golden.
Return the paneer, add soy sauce and chilli flakes and toss.
Finish with lemon juice and sesame.

tip.text: Broccoli is done when a knife slides into the stem easily. Mushy broccoli smells like a hostel corridor.

steps.text: Mix the chilli powder, coriander powder, crushed cumin, pepper and grated garlic with curd into a thick red paste.
Toss the paneer cubes in half the paste.
Heat half the ghee and sear the paneer until crusty. Take it out.
Add the rest of the ghee, the curry leaves and the remaining paste and fry on low until it darkens and smells roasted.
Add jaggery, salt, lemon and 2 tablespoons of water.
Return the paneer and toss until it's coated in the glossy red roast.

tip.text: Frying the paste slowly in ghee is the dish. Rush it and it tastes of raw chilli powder.

steps.text: Dice the carrots into small cubes the size of the peas.
Heat oil, add cumin and grated ginger.
Add the carrots, peas, turmeric and salt and stir well.
Cover and cook on low until the carrots are tender, stirring once or twice.
Uncover, add chilli and coriander powders and stir-fry 2 minutes.
Roll the sabzi into wraps warmed on the pan for a quick lunch.

tip.text: Same-size pieces cook evenly. Big carrot chunks will still be hard when the peas are mushy.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 150 ml water, covered, then move it to a tiffin.
Grate the beetroot on the large holes.
Crush the coconut, green chilli and garlic together in a folded paper.
Heat oil, pop the mustard seeds, add curry leaves, then the beetroot and salt.
Cover and cook on low, stirring now and then, until tender.
Add the coconut mixture and toss for 2 minutes until dry.

tip.text: Beetroot sweetens as it cooks. Taste and add a little more chilli if it's too sweet.

steps.text: Peel and cube the sweet potato.
Heat oil and cook the onion, garlic and ginger until soft.
Add chilli powder and turmeric, then the sweet potato and 200 ml water.
Cover and simmer until the sweet potato is tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the spinach, soy sauce and salt.
Warm through until the spinach wilts, then squeeze in the lemon.

tip.text: Once the coconut milk is in, keep it below a boil so it stays creamy.

steps.text: Boil the soya chunks, then drain, rinse cold and squeeze dry.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, lemon juice, chilli flakes and 3 tablespoons of hot water.
Fry the soya chunks in oil until the edges brown.
Add garlic, onion and capsicum and stir-fry for a minute.
Pour in the peanut sauce and toss until it coats everything.
Scatter crushed peanuts on top.

tip.text: Browning the soya first changes its texture from spongy to meaty.

steps.text: Bring 200 ml water to a boil in the pan with the crushed ginger and a pinch of black pepper.
Add the tea leaves and let them boil until the water turns dark.
Pour in the milk and sugar and stir once.
Bring it to a rolling boil, let it rise, lower the heat, and repeat twice.
Strain the chai through a tea strainer into two cups.

tip.text: Milk tea rises and boils over in seconds. Stay at the stove and lower the heat as it climbs.

steps.text: Pour the milk into the pan with the turmeric, a pinch of pepper and grated ginger.
Heat gently, stirring, until it steams and small bubbles form at the edge.
Switch off and stir in the jaggery.
Strain into a mug if you don't want the ginger bits.
Drink it warm, ideally half an hour before bed.

tip.text: Jaggery in boiling milk can curdle it. Add it after switching off.

steps.text: Chop the chocolate into small pieces.
Warm the milk in the pan until steaming, not boiling.
Add the chocolate, sugar and a pinch of instant coffee.
Whisk until the chocolate melts completely and the milk turns frothy.
Pour it into a mug while the froth is still on top.

tip.text: A tiny pinch of coffee doesn't make it taste of coffee. It makes the chocolate taste deeper.

steps.text: Dry-roast the makhana on low heat, stirring, until one crushed between your fingers snaps crisp.
Push the makhana aside and melt the ghee in the pan.
Add turmeric and chilli powder to the ghee and swirl for 10 seconds.
Toss the makhana in the spiced ghee until evenly coated.
Switch off, sprinkle chaat masala and salt, and let them cool to stay crunchy.

tip.text: Under-roasted makhana is chewy and sticks to your teeth. The crush test tells you it's ready.

steps.text: Dry-roast the thin poha on low heat, stirring, until it turns crisp and crunchy. Tip it into a bowl.
Heat the oil and fry the peanuts until they darken slightly.
Add roasted chana, mustard seeds, curry leaves and sliced green chilli and fry until crisp.
Add the turmeric, then switch off.
Tip the poha back in with salt and powdered sugar and toss until evenly yellow.
Cool completely and store in an airtight jar.

tip.text: Warm chivda sealed in a jar sweats and goes soft. Let it cool fully first.

steps.text: Rub the roasted peanuts between your palms to remove the skins, then halve them.
Grease a steel plate and the back of a steel bowl with ghee.
Melt the jaggery in the pan on low heat, stirring, until it bubbles and darkens slightly.
Drop a little into a cup of cold water. If it turns hard and snaps, it's ready.
Add the peanuts and stir fast to coat.
Tip onto the greased plate, flatten with the bowl and cut into squares while warm.

tip.text: If the jaggery drop stays soft, keep cooking. Under-cooked chikki stays chewy forever.

steps.text: Melt the ghee in the pan on low heat and add the besan.
Roast, stirring constantly, until it turns golden brown and smells nutty.
Tip it into a plate and let it cool until just warm.
Mix in the powdered sugar and chopped almonds.
Press handfuls tightly into 8 round laddoos.

tip.text: Low heat, constant stirring. Besan burns at the bottom while the top still looks raw.

steps.text: Toast the coconut on low heat for a couple of minutes until it smells fragrant.
Add the milk and sugar and stir to combine.
Cook, stirring, until the milk is absorbed and the mixture comes together.
Stir in the ghee and chopped cashews.
Cool slightly and roll into 10 small laddoos with greased palms.

tip.text: Stop when the mixture leaves the sides of the pan. Cooked further, the laddoos turn hard.

steps.text: Fry the vermicelli in ghee on low heat until golden. Push it aside.
Add the cashews, chopped almonds and raisins and fry until the raisins puff.
Pour in the milk and bring it to a boil, stirring.
Simmer, stirring every minute, until the vermicelli is soft and the milk thickens a little.
Add sugar and simmer 2 more minutes.
Eat it warm, or chill it in a closed box for the next day.

tip.text: Kheer thickens a lot as it cools. Leave it slightly runny in the pan.

steps.text: Peel and grate the carrots on the fine side of the grater.
Cook the grated carrot in the milk on medium, stirring often, until the milk is absorbed.
Add the sugar. It will turn wet again.
Keep stirring until it dries and turns glossy.
Add the ghee and chopped nuts and stir-fry for 2 minutes.

tip.text: Grate fine. Thick shreds take twice as long and never get that melting halwa texture.

steps.text: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into 1 cm thick rounds.
Arrange in a single layer in the oiled pan, cover, and cook on low until soft inside.
Uncover, turn the heat up and brown both sides.
Cut the rounds into cubes and put them in a bowl.
Toss with chaat masala, chilli, salt and lemon.
Top with pomegranate and coriander.

tip.text: Covered first, browned after. Sweet potato burns on the outside long before the inside softens.

steps.text: Cook the frozen corn in a splash of water in the pan until the water dries up.
Add the butter and the finely chopped garlic.
Fry on high, tossing, until some kernels char and pop.
Season with chilli powder and salt.
Squeeze lemon over and toss with coriander.

tip.text: Corn kernels can pop out of the pan. Keep a lid half on.

steps.text: Boil the potato cubes in salted water until just tender.
Drain and let them dry completely on a plate.
Fry the cubes in hot oil, turning, until crisp on all sides.
Toss with chaat masala, chilli powder, crushed cumin and salt.
Put them in a bowl with whisked curd, onion, lemon and coriander.
Scatter sev over the top right before eating.

tip.text: Boiled-then-fried gives a fluffy middle and crunchy outside, like the Delhi carts.

steps.text: Mix besan, rava, chilli powder, turmeric, hing and salt in a bowl.
Sprinkle a few drops of water over the peanuts and toss them in the besan mix until coated.
Shallow-fry the coated peanuts on medium, stirring, until the coating turns crisp and golden.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto a folded tissue.
Let them cool fully before eating, which is when they turn crunchy.

tip.text: Too much water makes the coating clump into balls. A few drops is all you need.

steps.text: Butter one side of each slice of bread.
Toast buttered side down until crisp.
Flip, lay chocolate pieces on the toasted side and cover the pan so they melt.
Spread the melted chocolate with the back of a spoon.
Top with banana slices and a drizzle of warm peanut butter.

tip.text: A lid melts the chocolate in a minute without moving it around.

steps.text: Rinse the sabudana and soak it in water.
Drain and add the sabudana to the milk in the pan.
Simmer, stirring, until the pearls turn clear and soft.
Add the sugar and simmer 2 minutes.
Fry the chopped cashews in ghee and pour them over.

tip.text: Sabudana sticks to the bottom. Stir every minute while it simmers.

steps.text: Roast the rava in ghee on low heat until golden.
Mash the banana and warm the milk in a separate cup.
Add the warm milk to the rava carefully and stir until absorbed.
Add the mashed banana and sugar.
Stir until the sheera is glossy and leaves the pan.
Top the sheera with roughly chopped cashews.

tip.text: Ripe, spotty bananas make the best sheera. Green ones taste starchy.

steps.text: Toast the oats dry in the pan on low until golden.
Tip them into a bowl and wipe the pan.
Warm the peanut butter and honey together on low, stirring, until runny.
Pour it over the oats with the chopped almonds and raisins and mix well.
Press firmly into a greased steel tiffin.
Chill until firm, then cut into 8 bars.

tip.text: Press hard with the back of a spoon. Loose bars crumble when you cut them.

steps.text: Boil the corn in a little water in the pan, then drain.
Melt the butter in the same pan and add the corn.
Toss with chaat masala, chilli powder and salt.
Switch off and stir in the onion, tomato and lemon.
Spoon into a cup and eat with a spoon.

tip.text: Raw onion and tomato go in off the heat, so they stay crunchy and fresh.

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs in the pan, then cool them in cold water and peel.
Halve the eggs lengthways and dust the cut sides with salt and chilli powder.
Whisk besan, rava, turmeric, the rest of the chilli powder and salt with about 3 tablespoons of water into a thick batter.
Dry the pan and heat the oil to about 5 mm deep.
Dip each egg half in the batter and fry, cut side down first, then turn, until golden all over.
Drain on a tissue and eat with chaat masala, raw onion and ketchup.

tip.text: Shallow oil is enough if you turn the pieces. Deep-frying in a small pan is how hostel fires start.
